title: Open questions, deferred systems
summary: What is still undecided, and what is deliberately waiting for a real need.

blocks.title: Open questions, deferred systems
blocks.body: Some things are undecided. Some things are decided to wait. Both are written down.

blocks.heading: Still open
items: Final mode names and behaviors - Present and Read, or Browse and Present.
Theme control - author-chosen only, or viewer auditioning stays.
Code home - keep the hosted prototype source as the baseline, then add a standalone toolchain only when its dependencies are defined.
Ownership and budget - repository policy, contributor model, hosting, and release rules.
The first real lesson to use as the acceptance case.

columns.name: Contributor workflow
columns.detail: Branches, previews, reviews and release checks - when a second contributor appears.

columns.name: Accounts and plans
columns.detail: Hosting permissions, previews and budgets - when deployment is real.

columns.name: Background execution
columns.detail: Runners and scheduled jobs - when a defined job needs them.

columns.name: Failure hardening
columns.detail: Allowlists, fixtures and drift checks - deepening as the stakes grow.

blocks.quote: Prefer one useful lesson and a second contribution that proves reuse. Visual polish should help comprehension, not consume the build.

blocks.title: Deferred means deferred
blocks.body: These sections are reference, not gates. The trigger to revisit is a real second contributor or a real runner, not anxiety.

blocks.title: Deferral rule
blocks.body: Revisit deferred systems when a real contributor, deployment, or background job creates a concrete need.

blocks.heading: Keep the plan where it can break
blocks.body: The plan lives inside the product now. Using it is how the weak parts get found.
